text:
elena (PM): Drafted a PRD stub for the compliance/audit evidence work — covers audit log granularity, KMS/HSM integration patterns, exportable evidence packs, and launch gating. Sharing draft: https://redwood.internal/prd/compliance-evidence. Need to converge on minimal must-haves vs nice-to-haves; customers are asking for 7y retention and HSM-backed keys. Ping @kevin @maria @nisha for security/eng/compliance input. TL;DR: goal is a shipping-safe baseline for Hosted + Dedicated, with optional on-prem/HSM add-ons.

kevin (Security): +1. From a security standpoint we need: tamper-evident append-only logs, KMS call traces (who/what/when), key rotation and destruction events, and a snapshot of key access policies for the evidence pack. For HSMs, we need a clear attestation of HSM-backed wrapping for export-critical operations. Concern: 7y retention is expensive and increases attack window. Recommend default 1y retention, with paid extended retention. Also we should define SLOs for log delivery (suggest <30s) and a canonical event schema.

maria (Eng): A couple of clarifications: are we expected to log per-token data? that's going to explode cost and complexity. My suggestion: capture request metadata, model_id, model_version, route, decision (eg fallback), and a pointer to stored request content only when the customer opts in to full-evidence. Edge cases: streaming sessions and KV-cache diffs — for audits we may need to reconstruct cache state for a given session; that's nontrivial and should be scoped as an advanced feature.

aj (Infra): From infra ops: HSM integration latency is real. Sync HSM unwrap/wrap on the hot path adds ~40–200ms depending on vendor and region. If we mandate HSM ops inline we risk breaking our latency SLOs. Proposal: low-latency path uses transient local wrapping keys that are periodically sealed by the HSM (async seal). For auditability, emit an attest log to prove HSM sealed the key. Example retention config (prototype):

```
audit:
  retention_days: 365
  storage_tier: standard
  compress: true
  encryption: customer_kms
```

Also: consider storage tiering for extended retention and a separate export pipeline for evidence packs.

nisha (Compliance): For SOC2/ISO evidence expectations: we need chain-of-custody, integrity hashes on exportable bundles, and the ability to produce a time-scoped evidence pack (eg 90-day sample or full period on request). Acceptance criteria proposal: (1) exportable evidence pack with integrity hash and manifest; (2) immutable append-only logs with enforced retention and deletion controls; (3) KMS audit trail showing key creation/rotation/destruction with principal identity; (4) documented evidence request playbook. Edge case: legal holds — customers must be able to request retention override; require controls and an approval log.

elena (PM): Nice. Action items: kevin — draft canonical event type list (due EOD Wed); maria — estimate cost and latency delta for capturing per-request metadata vs per-token logs (due Fri); aj — prototype async HSM seal pattern + sample retention config; nisha — draft SOC2 evidence acceptance checklist. I'll fold into PRD and push an updated doc for review. Quick poll for default retention: react :one: for 1y, :three: for 3y, :seven: for 7y.

deploy-bot: Deployment started for branch prd/compliance-evidence — CI: ✅, infra checks: pending.

maria (Eng): quick follow-up — if we support customer-managed KMS we must also support key rotation windows and a migration path to avoid long-term decrypt failures; add a migration tool + automated verification to scope.

kevin (Security): One more note: call out the threat model in the PRD (rogue admin, compromised backup snapshot, compromised HSM). Acceptance criteria should include periodic key-use summaries and the ability to export key-access logs scoped to an auditor query.

elena (PM): Thanks everyone — I'll incorporate these changes and schedule a focused RFC review next Tue. If you have a strong preference on default retention please leave a one-line reply here.
